notes.title: Pre-make Update #2!!!
notes.notes:
Hey, guys. Last BeNeVoLeNcE, here...

I know this is WAY earlier than expected but I SOMEHOW pulled it off just YESTERDAY...

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExa3BsN3J6dHN2bWJoNjE3YnprMWw1bWtleGQ0YnEzcnMxYmJueDcxaCZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/Fqcjg5EACFK6zwFYHi/giphy-downsized-large.gif[/img]

[h1]WIDESCREEN IS HERE!!![/h1]

To get it working, I blended some modified scripts from the Prologue Demo for "The T.O.T.E." and ran some tests! When I found that it was working, I just had to adjust different story scenes and graphics used for certain parts of the game and then it just worked!

I've been testing it since yesterday and it seems to work pretty well--even better than the Prologue Demo. 

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/WOGfBmT6ATKAueJ7pW/giphy.gif[/img]

It's not perfect, and it probably never will be but it sure is better than those ugly black bars on the side. Lol Plus, if you have a Steam Deck to try it on, it'll have thinner horizontal bars on the top and bottom that make it look way more cinematic. Pretty cool stuff.

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/B5BS5Pw3odH2PNg9aH/giphy.gif[/img]

Now, the only slight issue is that there might be some unexpected bugs or even unintended camera angles in the game due to the changing of the base resolution. I'll probably just continue enjoying my playthrough on the Steam Deck so if I spot anything glaring, I'll be sure to patch it all up now that I have all of the files organized and ready for bug fixes again. Feel free to post in the community threads to let me know if you notice anything is off as well. You guys have definitely helped a lot with that up until now.


Here are some smaller fixes that are coming with this update: 

Fixed Mega Ran's attack AGAIN so that it now destroys bushes (it was only working on pots and boxes before).*
Changed the Black Mic's backstory scenes at the beginning of the game to the way they were in the earlier versions of the Prologue demo so that they are more cinematic. 
Changed the UI font to a more readable, chunkier font. 
Resized the UI font. 

*Quick note on Mega Ran's basic attack: It now goes through walls. I remember this being a complaint before concerning him being "OP" but I'd like to test out if this will REALLY affect the game's balance enough for it to be a serious problem.

I'm also aware that there are some strange differences in the font sizes for the UI (ie, the 1st player's health vs. the followers' health). I'll be looking into those later.



Hope you guys enjoy this update as well as the last one! 

- LB

notes.title: Pre-make Update #1
notes.notes:
Hey, guys. Last BeNeVoLeNcE here--

I just released an update for Tales of the Elements that you may find interesting!

Details below!


[b]~ SINGLE MODE ADDED ~[/b]

Are you TIRED of your AI members constantly running off into their deaths? Can't seem to figure out how to configure them to heal and keep themselves alive?

Well, in this new update, I added a quality-of-life feature called "Single Mode." 

This mode is a single-player mode that DISABLES your party members in areas where there are enemies so that the selected character that you are controlling is the only one one the map during battles. 

Any character in your current party can still be selected from the character select menu. Whoever is in your party at the time will also still gain experience.

Single mode can be toggled from the in-game sub menu.

IMPORTANT: When toggled ON, this feature will ONLY become activate at the next time an area with enemies is entered into so it's best to activate when in-town or in an area without enemies.


[b]~ Cloud Saves now supported! ~[/b]

I'm actually late to announcing this as I had shadow dropped this to the game awhile back. Cloud Saves are now working across all devices!



[b]~ Testing for Steam Deck ~[/b]

I've been playing through the game here and there on my Steam Deck to make note of some details to further development of the new remake, The T.O.T.E., which I'm planning to launch hopefully this summer.

So far, the game runs REALLY well on the Steam Deck with only a slight blow to performance on 1 or 2 of the 3D special stages. 

So, if you were a fan and enjoyed playing Tales of the Elements, try giving it a try with the new updates on your Steam Deck and be sure to leave whatever feedback you can so that we can get Steam to test this game for Steam Deck Verification!



Thanks for all of your guys' support and patience. 

This game was my first game release as a (mostly) solo developer so it's important to me. With that being said, expect a couple of updates going forward as I continue developing the remake "The T.O.T.E.!"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Update fix log:
Fixed the early game "rhyme writing" tutorial not displaying correctly. 
Fixed the satellite switch on the 2F so that it's displaying correctly before being destroyed.
Fixed the Flower Girl transaction in the base game so that it now gives the correct item when standing on the left.
Fixed Mega Ran's basic weapon attack not being able to shoot through breakable objects such as bushes, pots, boxes, etc.*
Added a short bit of dialogue to wrap up and the beginning of the "sky bloom" side quest.
Edited a slight typo where "BeNeVoLeNcE" says "lock down" instead of "lockdown" right before the Treeble radio station boss.

*This will not work on current loaded equipment from previously saved data. So, you'll need to get a new weapon for Mega Ran added into your inventory or you'll need to start a new game. Either of those will work.

OTHER changes:
Removed beginning video from game as it was an early concept video that no longer adds any meaningful context, supports or conveys the proper plot points brought out in the story (can be still viewed from within game files).
Added the option to toggle on or off the new Single Mode when starting a new game.
Also removed the opening text scroll from the game. 


Plans for next update(s):

Remake soundtrack BGMs 
Dialogue fixes and adjustments to vague objectives within a certain main story task that happens to mostly take place in a desert-y area....
Maybe something else...


- LB

notes.title: Tales of the Elements 2nd Chapter is HERE!
notes.notes:
Hey, guys!

Last BeNeVoLeNcE--

I'm really pleased to announce the release of the 2nd Chapter of Tales of the Elements!

You can find it on the Steam Store right here:
http://store.steampowered.com/app/779720/Tales_of_the_Elements__2nd_Chapter/

If you're curious to know what this 2nd Chapter is about--No problem! But, first--It might be a little easier for me to share a bit of the story behind the project as a whole, first. So, here's what we got:

Tales of the Elements was produced and recorded back in 2015 as 2 separate Hip Hop albums. The concept of it was that each album would be like a separate "disc" that made up a full JRPG like they did with most JRPG games back on the first Playstation.

Once we finished we decided to make them into 2 episodic games but after some time, those games turned into a single game with the second part being DLC for the main game. 

Why would I recommend 2nd Chapter?

You can think of 2nd Chapter like as if it's your "second disc." With it, you can experience the full story and side content as well--It literally has the same amount of content as the First Chapter (the main game)!

But, there are a couple of ways that you can get it:

You can get 2nd Chapter by itself (see the link above) or you can get it bundled together at a discount with the album right here on Steam!:

http://store.steampowered.com/bundle/5922/Tales_of_the_Elements_2C__Full_Story/


Or--if you haven't gotten the main game yet--You can get both chapters (including their albums) all in one bundle at a discount here:

http://store.steampowered.com/bundle/5924/Tales_of_the_Elements__Complete/


This has been a real passion project for me and I really appreciate everyone who's contributed and supported it!

Thanks and again--Feel free to contact me directly or post up here for any questions that are Tales of the Elements related!


- LB

notes.title: Tales of the Elements 2nd Chapter Coming Soon! (Big FC Update, too!)
notes.notes:
Hello, everyone!

This is Last BeNeVoLeNcE and I have some great news!


First off, the issue that some of us were experiencing with the game installing itself as an empty folder has been fixed! So, the new update for the game is fully tested and working! I apologize for any inconvenience that issue may have caused in the last couple of days.

Second, Tales of the Elements 2nd Chapter is finally coming out on February 9th and you can even check out the trailer and screenshots in the store!: 
http://store.steampowered.com/app/779720/Tales_of_the_Elements__2nd_Chapter/

The 2nd Chapter will include a bunch of new content--The second half of the story, 2 new playable characters, new locations, new special stages, several different endgame sidequests, and secret bosses! 

That's not even the best part--even though it will DOUBLE the content of the base game, the price is set to be only $3.99! 

How come?

This is because the Tales of the Elements 2C album will be completely optional and will be available for purchasing separately or together with the game. And of course, it will be only $2.99.


Third--After finishing up 2C, I've added in a new update for FC which fixes several different bugs as well as adds in the hand drawn art used in the maps of 2C (Drawn by Snowberry, the same artist who's done the cover artwork for 2C's album)!

There have also been some changes to the game's systems. For one, BeNeVoLeNcE's "Sample-flip" ability is now useable through one single skill instead of being available as 3 different skills. This is more convenient for players because there's no need to switch skills when trying to use the sample-flip that corresponds to whatever is equipped to BeNeVoLeNcE's secondary equipment/weapon slot.


I'm really looking forward to the release of 2C as it brings a lot of much needed improvements, content, and enhancements to the game!

As always, thank you guys for your support and if you have any questions or if you find any bugs--feel free to post up in the community forums or send me a message anytime!

Edit:

I received a bit of feedback and I thought it would be a good idea to address some concerns right here:

I intended to release the "2nd Chapter" with some new achievements to unlock but there was no way to do that besides adding it to the base game's achievement stats. 

But after receiving some much-needed feedback, I realize that it wasn't a good idea so I've decided to remove the achievements for 2C. All of the achievements are now fully unlockable in FC alone! Hopefully this is a positive development for our completionists!

Also:

The "2nd Chapter" DLC is separate from the main game to match the albums' releases. They're meant to be episodic with FC as the first game and album then 2C continuing as the DLC and second album. Hopefully that clears some things up! 

For any questions about it--feel free to post up here in the community or email me at: lastbenevolence@outlook.com! 

Thanks!

- LB

notes.title: Big Changes (Free update!)
notes.notes:
Hey, everybody! 

Last BeNeVoLeNcE, here:


In the recent months, I've began working on Tales of the Elements 2C. The story's already written, the album is already recorded, and all of the new features and gameplay enhancements for 2C are already complete!

So, while working on those new features, I decided it would be a good idea to make all of the new features and gameplay balances available in FC as part of a FREE update! 

This update's big because it's really taking all of the new ideas that will be used in 2C and completely giving FC a makeover with them. 


Aside from some minor bug fixes--here's what's new:

In-depth (but completely optional) tutorials for important game features.
Eight (8) "special stages" (mini-games) to unlock special inspiration.
Voice grunts for dialogue from main characters as well as some NPCs.
Battle voiceovers for playable characters.
Breakable boxes, barrels, and chests with random item drops (replacing chests).

New splash screens before the title.
New title screen and new title screen music.
New windowskin for dialogue.
Updated sub menu. 


Next up?

Finishing 2C!

Stay tuned....



- LB

notes.title: Getting ready for the 2nd Chapter!
notes.notes:
Hey, everyone!  

Last BeNeVoLeNcE, here--

First off, I'd like to sincerely thank everyone who's supported this release as developing this game was a real "life achievement" for me to personally unlock. It was always a goal since I was young to get into game development and I never thought it would have been possible to develop games on my own. So, seriously, thank you all for your support! There's more to come!

But, that's not what this announcement is about--

I'm happy to reveal that Tales of the Elements - 2nd Chapter is currently in development! Actually, to be honest, it's been in-development for quite some time now!

You're probably wondering what you can look forward to seeing in 2nd Chapter and as I can't say too much just yet--I can share a few quick points:

- Tales of the Elements - 2nd Chapter is the second HALF of the story while FC was the first half. That means that when FC and 2C come together, you can enjoy the complete experience of the Tales of the Elements story!

- It goes without saying that there will be new music, new places, new equipment, new skills, & new characters!

- Just like before, the album will be released at the same time as the game.

Just recently, I put out an update for the game here on Steam in preparation for the 2nd half of the story. 

The update has a number of adjustments ranging from not-so-big to pretty major. But, here are some notable things to keep in mind:

The levels in which characters learn skills have been readjusted to give the game a bit more balance, challenge, and most of all--to accommodate the 2nd Chapter. This means that characters will be learning some of their skills at higher levels than before. (Example: if DJ's were learning a skill at level 5 before, now they are learning that skill at level 14.) 

I understand that this may come as a disappointment to some but I found that this was a better way to give time before characters learn all of their skills in the game--and this is all with a view of how long the game will be once the 2nd Chapter is added to the game. Besides that, it keeps players from being too overpowered towards the end of FC.

With that being said, this also means that some characters have NEW skills. Technically, most of these skills are meant to be learned in 2C. But, if you spend enough time in the unlockable dungeon (in FC), you MIGHT get to the point of leveling up enough to earn those skills!

Another notable change--There are now descriptions for EVERY skill in the game. 

Some skill animations have been adjusted such as the animation for when the microphone blades hit enemies. 

Some more changes: Snowberry's weapon was changed from "gloves" to "Drawing Pens." She can still use "gloves" but she starts off with a pen. Also, all of her skills have been renamed. 

There have also been some visual updates to some of the maps as well as some minor bug fixes.


Myself, as well as the artists who contributed to both albums, and Randombeats Music are all excited to bring you Tales of the Elements 2nd Chapter!

 Soon, we'll have more information on 2C's release but in the meantime-- 
stay tuned!


- LB

This means that characters will be learning some of their skills at higher levels than before. (Example: if DJ's were learning a skill at level 5 before, now they are learning that skill at level 14.) 

I understand that this may come as a disappointment to some but I found that this was a better way to give time before characters learn all of their skills in the game--and this is all with a view of how long the game will be once the 2nd Chapter is added to the game. Besides that, it keeps players from being too overpowered towards the end of FC.

With that being said, this also means that some characters have NEW skills. Technically, most of these skills are meant to be learned in 2C. But, if you spend enough time in the unlockable dungeon (in FC), you MIGHT get to the point of leveling up enough to earn those skills!

Another notable change--There are now descriptions for EVERY skill in the game. 

Some skill animations have been adjusted such as the animation for when the microphone blades hit enemies. 

Some more changes: Snowberry's weapon was changed from "gloves" to "Drawing Pens." She can still use "gloves" but she starts off with a pen. Also, all of her skills have been renamed. 

There have also been some visual updates to some of the maps as well as some minor bug fixes.


Myself, as well as the artists who contributed to both albums, and Randombeats Music are all excited to bring you Tales of the Elements 2nd Chapter!

 Soon, we'll have more information on 2C's release but in the meantime-- 
stay tuned!


- LB

notes.title: TOTEFC Steam Update Patch Notes
notes.notes:
Here's everything that was changed, fixed, and added in this update:


Added a system menu with options for volume, auto-dashing, and fullscreen.

Pre-edited .ini file to run the game at fullscreen automatically at first start-up for new players.

Fixed a time-system issue with the Snowberry date.

Fixed a bug where the player could still play the record smash mini-game after the date.

Improved the ai so that ranged attackers and healers distance themselves from enemies.

Weakened Mega Ran's hookshot damage.

Fixed Mega Ran's normal attack so that he can only shoot through walls with charged attacks

Changed Mega Ran's Skills so that they all require TP. 

Rebalanced the Fenix Down drops at the beginning of the game to indirectly fix an issue where the player could possibly get stuck forever between two boulders if Mega Ran died and the game was saved.

Raised the health stat on a number of late-game bosses to balance against stronger follower AI.

Raised TP cost of Skills that use TP and added in auto-regeneration for all characters who specialize in TP-based attacks except for the secret character.

Removed the auto-lock on the Allegory doors.

Added an explanation of the stats and attack function of the samples.

Added new custom NPCs throughout the entire game.

Added achievements

Added new map tileset pieces and edited some existing ones.

Added K-Murdock as an unlockable character.

Added 3 new key items.

Changed the requirement for leaving The Estate.

Added new hand-drawn character portraits for all of the playable characters and for one non-playable character.

Added antidotes to Traxx's general store.



- LB

notes.title: TOTEFC Steam Update & Winter Sale!!!
notes.notes:
Hey, guys!

Last B., here!

Tales of the Elements FC will be on sale for only $3.49 during the entire Steam Winter Sale! But, that's not all...

Just as promised, we've finally completed the "Special Steam Update," just in time for the sale!


For those who haven't heard about this update, here's what it's about:

Basically, at the time of release, there were ideas that were pushed forward by the community. Turned out, we liked them so much that we went ahead and pushed bits and pieces of those ideas into the First Chapter of this game to set the stage for development of the Second Chapter. 

Think of it as a FREE "mini-expansion" that adds a little more content and flavor to the game! 

We also took note of all of the issues that were found in-game by different players and we've included those bug fixes in this update!


Here are some things to look forward to in this update:

K-Murdock as an unlockable character!
New hand-drawn main character portraits!
Redesigned map artwork!
Steam Achievements!



To address some technical concerns we've added:

Improved follower AI - Long-range attacker = Attacks from a distance!
Revamped NPCs
An easily accessible "System" menu - With a fullscreen option!



We hope you guys enjoy the free update and if you have any questions, concerns, or bug reports feel free to contact us in the community feed!

Thanks for your support!



- LB

PS. We'll also be posting the patch notes in a separate announcement.

notes.title: About TOTE FAQ
notes.notes:
Hey, everyone!

Because a lot of users may not be familiar with the album that this game is based off of, I thought it would be a good idea to put together a FAQ to answer any questions (or concerns) that might come up about the project!

So, let’s get started!


[b][u]"You keep mentioning this 'album of the same name.' Why is that?"[/u][/b]
Tales of the Elements FC is a Jazzy-Hip Hop album that I produced and recorded alongside Mega Ran and K-Murdock, who are best known for their video game tribute album “Forever Famicom.” It has a story concept where each of us who recorded had role-played like we were in a Japanese Role Playing game. On top of that, I came up with a backstory for the album where the story of the 4 elements of Hip Hop were re-imagined in a fantasy setting like any other JRPG.  
The album is the “source material” for the game so it’s completely based off of that story I wrote for the album.


[b][u]"Why did you choose to use RPG Maker?"[/u][/b]
When we first started working on the album we weren’t planning on making a game alongside it. The idea for a game literally came after we were already finished producing and recording the album over the span of 2 years! Since the album was so close to being ready for release, I thought it would be a good idea to use an engine that I was already familiar with using and one that would be more appropriate for the scope of the project. In other words, the game was only meant to be played as an extension of the album and not as a game on it’s own. The idea to release on Steam came to us just a month ago!
Feel free to check out the album on iTunes, Spotify, Bandcamp, or the Google Play Store! 


[b][u]"But, it’s RPG Maker and the sprites are generic."[/u][/b]
RPG Maker isn't a sign of "lazy development" and it definitely isn't an automatic sign of bad games, either. I know my way around the engine because I've been messing with it for YEARS now. It also comes with graphic assets (just like Unity and Unreal does). It specifically works for making RPGs and that's what we needed for this project so naturally, it's what I chose to use. That aside, it was still a lot of work to create what I did with that engine. The development time for the game is sitting at 1400+ hours. Of course, that was spread across about a year and a few months of time.
As for the sprites I would really like to replace the map sprites (at least) as soon as possible. Anything to make this project better I’m interested in looking into! Also, Glen and I have been talking about porting the game to Unity or another engine in general. If we do that, we'll have to replace all of the sprites with new ones, anyway.


[b][u]"'Tales Of?' Isn't that a ripoff of another game series? (Symphonia, Berseria)"[/u][/b]
No. This project is not related to any of those titles.


[b][u]"So, why did you pick the name 'Tales of the Elements?'”[/u][/b]
When I first started recording the album I wanted to make an album that told the story of Hip Hop in a way that was like a JRPG. To make that theme clear, I came up with a name that sounded like a JRPG title. I could've probably said "Legend of the Elements" or something like that but "Tales of the Elements" sounded right to me. Plus, the album’s concept was meant to be a major tribute to RPGs like Tales of Symphonia, Final Fantasy, Secret of Mana, etc. 
If I knew from the beginning that we were going to be pushing a fully realized game out on Steam with the album I wouldn't have needed the title to be such an obvious nod to JRPGs and I would've done the same as I did with my first album "Save the World,"  which was also a nod to JRPGs but the theme wasn't as obvious as I wanted it to be, hence why I made it more obvious with this title.


[b][u]"Aren't you afraid of a lawsuit?"[/u][/b]
The possibility of lawsuit was brought up actually. We looked into it and the "Tales of" games actually have the [i]full[/i] name trademarked; not just the "Tales of" part. We also located many games and other projects that start with the same term that have had no issues, so we're not worried.


[b][u]"So, what’s up with the 'FC' in the title?"[/u][/b]
“FC” stands for “First Chapter.” This is a release of the first of two parts. Funny story about that: we originally thought of using “Disc 1” but since iTunes wouldn’t allow us to upload artwork with a reference to physical packaging, I had to think of something fast; so I thought “First Chapter” would continue the project’s “trend” of dropping JRPG-inspired references.


[b][u]"What about the cover artwork for Tales of the Elements FC? It looks familiar…."[/u][/b]
Oh, yeah! It was done by Daniel Hill (Danji’s Designs) and the inspiration for it was taken from a piece of artwork used in Xenoblade Chronicles.



Glad to be able to answer any questions so if you have more, so feel free to start up a thread in the community hub or shoot me an email!

Thanks for reading!
